#+TITLE: CXD

* Overview

CXD is a C++20 library for two-dimensional and three-dimensional convex
collision detection. It implements the Gilbert-Johnson-Keerthi (GJK) algorithm
for intersection tests and the Expanding Polytope Algorithm (EPA) for penetration
information.

The library is adapter-based and supports floating-point vectors from
the C++ standard library, Boost.uBLAS, Eigen. The standalone
benchmarks also exercise the Siconos vector type, which is implemented
with Eigen in the pinned Siconos release.

* Collision API

=gjk_inter= accepts two non-empty collections of floating-point vectors and a
non-zero initial direction. For 2D, pass two-dimensional vectors; for 3D, pass
three-dimensional vectors and use the explicit =gjk_inter<3>= overload. It
accepts an optional =cxd::gjk_options= value with a positive tolerance and a
bounded iteration count. Invalid inputs raise =std::invalid_argument=; a search
that exceeds its iteration limit raises =std::runtime_error=. A repeated support
point reports separation because the search cannot make further progress.

=epa= requires a non-degenerate triangle simplex returned by GJK. It expands
the complete Minkowski-difference polytope, selecting the globally closest
edge to the origin on each iteration. Its tolerance and iteration count must
be positive.

* Broad phase

=broad_phase(shapes)= uses sweep-and-prune over axis-aligned bounding boxes and
returns index pairs whose boxes overlap, including edge-touching boxes. The
library parameterizes the dimension, so the same broad phase works for both
2D and 3D shape collections. It is a conservative filter, not a collision test:
every returned pair must still be passed to =gjk_inter=, while pairs absent
from the result are definitely separated. Pass a non-negative padding distance
as =broad_phase(shapes, padding)= to retain nearby pairs, for predictive
time-stepping contact detection.

* Reproducible Guix workflow

All commands below use the pinned channels in
=siconos-2026-08-12.scm= and a pure Guix environment. Evaluate the directory
setup block once before the compiler-specific blocks. Each Babel block uses
=:results none= so evaluating it never writes command output to this file.

#+name: cxd-create-build-directories
#+begin_src sh :compile :results none :exports code
  # Keep compiler builds and benchmark artifacts out of the source directories.
  guix time-machine -C siconos-2026-08-12.scm -- \
       environment --pure --ad-hoc coreutils -- \
       mkdir -p build-gcc build-clang benchmarks-build build-demo build-demo-siconos build-demo-3d build-demo-3d-siconos
#+end_src

** GCC: configure, build, and test

The GCC commands configure an out-of-tree Debug build in =build-gcc=. Run the
three blocks in order. The configure step builds the library and its tests;
the standalone benchmarks are configured separately (see below) and are added
to the root project only with =-DCXD_BUILD_BENCHMARKS=ON=, which additionally
requires Siconos, Google Benchmark, and Eigen in the same profile.

#+name: cxd-cmake-gcc
#+header: :var mk=(progn (mkdir "build-gcc" t) "")
#+header: :dir build-gcc
#+begin_src sh :compile :results none :exports code
  # Configure the root CMake project with the pinned GCC toolchain.
  guix time-machine -C ../siconos-2026-08-12.scm -- \
       shell --pure \
       gcc-toolchain make cmake cppunit boost dash -- \
       dash -c "CC=gcc CXX=g++ cmake -U CMAKE_C_COMPILER -U CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER -U CMAKE_MAKE_PROGRAM \
       -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug .."
#+end_src

#+header: :var mk=(progn (mkdir "build-gcc" t) "")

#+header: :var mk=(progn (mkdir "build-gcc" t) "")

       make test
#+end_src

* Device backend (CUDA, opt-in)

Phase 5 of the GPU roadmap ships a CUDA backend behind the phase-3 batch
memory contract, graded against the phase-4 golden parity files. It is
strictly opt-in: the header-only library never requires CUDA, and the
default build is byte-identical without it.

Code lives under =src/device/=:
- =src/device/cxd_batch_device.cuh= — thread-per-pair GJK and EPA kernels
  for 2D and 3D, ported line-for-line from the host batch reference
  (=src/cxd_batch.hpp=), with the two-pass pipeline (device GJK
  statuses+seeds, host compaction of the hit list, device EPA over the
  hits) and POD result rows: =cxd_dev_gjk_row= carries status and seed,
  =cxd_dev_answer= carries penetration depth and contact normal, with NaN
  in place wherever the device refuses (arena cap trips).
- =src/device/cxd_device_test.cu= — =t_device_golden_parity=, which runs
  the full shared corpus for {double, float} × {2D, 3D} against the
  committed goldens in =src/test/golden/=: statuses exact, depths and
  normals inside the same bands the host batch uses (1e-6 depth / 1e-4
  rad angle for double, 1e-4 / 1e-3 for float), and refusals required to
  answer NaN. No tolerance is widened for the device.

Configure with =-DCXD_BUILD_DEVICE=ON=. The device TU is C++17 and never
includes the core headers, so nvcc 12.0 works; it needs a host compiler
nvcc accepts (clang++-14 validated — nvcc rejects gcc 13+ at this
toolkit), the CUDA architectures default to =sm_86=, and the compile
sets =--expt-relaxed-constexpr -fmad=false=. Both flags are load-bearing:
relaxed constexpr is required by device-side =std::array= use, and the
fmad switch keeps float GJK decisions on the strict-IEEE path the Debug
host build computed the goldens with.

#+begin_src sh :compile :results none :exports code
  # Build the device parity test and run the full suite (59 host + 1 device test).
  cmake -S . -B build-device -DCXD_BUILD_DEVICE=ON \
        -DCXD_CUDA_HOST_COMPILER=clang++-14 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug
  cmake --build build-device -j8
  (cd build-device && ctest)
#+end_src

The remaining phase-5 work (warp-per-pair kernels, prefix-sum/atomic hit
lists, ns/pair numbers) is tracked in
[[file:docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-11-gpu-roadmap.md][the GPU roadmap]].

* Benchmarks

The standalone =benchmark/= CMake project uses Google Benchmark to measure
two-dimensional vector inner products and complete GJK intersection queries.
It compares the STL vector and array adapters, Boost.uBLAS, Siconos/Eigen, and
the fixed-point adapter. Fixtures use deterministic non-zero inputs; every GJK
iteration checks one separated and one intersecting shape pair.

Benchmarks are not correctness tests and are intentionally outside the main
CMake project. Run them in =Release= mode, retain the JSON artifact, and
compare results only on the same machine under similar load and CPU-frequency
conditions. The JSON output is ignored by Git. Detailed GCC and Clang variants
are available in [[file:benchmark/README.org][benchmark/README.org]].

The following GCC blocks configure, build, and run the benchmarks from the
dedicated =benchmarks-build= directory. Run them in order after evaluating
=cxd-create-build-directories=.

#+name: cxd-benchmark-cmake-gcc
#+header: :var mk=(progn (mkdir "benchmarks-build" t) "")
#+header: :dir benchmarks-build
#+begin_src sh :compile :results none :exports code
  # Configure the standalone benchmark project for optimized measurements.
  guix time-machine -C ../siconos-2026-08-12.scm -- \
       shell --pure \
       siconos benchmark gcc-toolchain boost cmake make eigen dash -- \
       dash -c "cmake ../benchmark -DSICONOS_INSTALL_DIR=\${GUIX_ENVIRONMENT} \
       -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release"
#+end_src

#+name: cxd-benchmark-make-gcc
#+header: :var mk=(progn (mkdir "benchmarks-build" t) "")
#+header: :dir benchmarks-build
#+begin_src sh :compile :results none :exports code
  # Build the standalone benchmark executable.
  guix time-machine -C ../siconos-2026-08-12.scm -- \
       shell --pure \
       siconos benchmark gcc-toolchain boost cmake make eigen dash -- \
       make VERBOSE=0 -j4
#+end_src

#+name: cxd-benchmark-run-gcc
#+header: :var mk=(progn (mkdir "benchmarks-build" t) "")
#+header: :dir benchmarks-build
#+begin_src sh :compile :results none :exports code
  # Save aggregate statistics from ten repetitions as an ignored JSON artifact.
  guix time-machine -C ../siconos-2026-08-12.scm -- \
       shell --pure \
       siconos benchmark gcc-toolchain boost cmake make eigen dash -- \
       ./bench1 --benchmark_repetitions=10 --benchmark_report_aggregates_only=true \
       --benchmark_out=bench1.json --benchmark_out_format=json
#+end_src

* Visual regression cases

[[file:visualization/gjk_cases.svg][GJK 2D visual fixture sheet]] and
[[file:visualization/gjk_3d_cases.svg][GJK/EPA 3D visual fixture sheet]]

Both sheets are *generated*, not hand-authored. Their shapes and outcomes
come from a runtime JSON dump printed by the (CTest-uncounted, manually
invoked) CppUnit test =Test::t_dump_visualization_cases= (=src/test/test.cpp=),
which reuses the exact same shape-construction helpers
(=make_gjk_2d_geometric_cases=, =make_gjk_3d_geometric_cases=,
=make_gjk_3d_tetrahedron_reduction_shapes=,
=make_epa_3d_penetration_exact_shapes=) and =cxd::gjk_inter=/=cxd::gjk_inter<3>=/
=cxd::epa= calls as =t_gjk_geometric_cases=, =t_gjk_3d_geometric_cases=,
=t_gjk_3d_tetrahedron_reduction=, and =t_epa_3d_penetration_exact=, and
asserts the same expected outcomes before printing them.
=visualization/render_gjk_2d_cases.py= and =render_gjk_3d_cases.py= only
project and draw those numbers, so neither figure can show a shape or a
result the tests don't actually exercise.

Blue is shape A, orange is shape B, and the badge is the actual (not merely
expected) GJK intersection result. The 3D sheet uses a trimetric projection
(deliberately not true isometric -- several cases there are offset from shape
A by a pure =(1,1,1)=-direction translation, which true isometric projects to
zero) with each panel independently scaled to fill its frame, so distances
are not comparable across 3D panels; the 2D sheet uses one scale (up to 1
unit = 80px) shrunk per panel only when a case's extent doesn't fit.

#+name: cxd-generate-gjk-visualization
#+header: :var mk=(progn (mkdir "build-gcc" t) "")
#+header: :dir build-gcc
#+begin_src sh :compile :results none :exports code
  # Rebuild the test binary, dump the geometric cases it actually computes,
  # regenerate both SVGs from that dump, and fail if either committed file
  # is stale relative to what the tests currently compute.
  guix time-machine -C ../siconos-2026-08-12.scm -- \
       shell --pure \
       gcc-toolchain make cmake coreutils grep openmpi openssh boost-mpi cppunit eigen python git dash -- \
       dash -c "make VERBOSE=0 -j4 cxd_test && \
       ./src/test/cxd_test Test::t_dump_visualization_cases > /tmp/cxd_gjk_dump.txt && \
       python3 ../visualization/render_gjk_2d_cases.py /tmp/cxd_gjk_dump.txt ../visualization/gjk_cases.svg && \
       python3 ../visualization/render_gjk_3d_cases.py /tmp/cxd_gjk_dump.txt ../visualization/gjk_3d_cases.svg && \
       python3 -c \"import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET; ET.parse('../visualization/gjk_cases.svg'); ET.parse('../visualization/gjk_3d_cases.svg')\" && \
       cd .. && git --no-pager diff --exit-code visualization/gjk_cases.svg visualization/gjk_3d_cases.svg"
#+end_src

* Interactive visual demo

=demo/= is a native raylib application that simulates several convex
two-dimensional bodies in a box. CXD sweep-and-prune finds candidate body
pairs and GJK detects the overlapping pairs; a small sequential impulse solver
applies restitution and positional correction.
Red lines start at the centroid of the convex overlap region and show the
collision normals used by the solver. The demo is purposely rudimentary: it
has no friction, angular collision impulse, or continuous collision detection.

Evaluate =cxd-create-build-directories= first, then configure, build, test,
and run the standalone demo from =build-demo=. The run block requires an active
desktop display. =--bodies N= selects the number of dynamic bodies (default:
16); =--frames N= is useful for a finite headless run. Press =Space= to pause,
=R= to reset, and =Esc= to close.

* Interactive 3D visual demo

=demo-3d/= is a native raylib application that simulates several convex
three-dimensional bodies in a box. CXD sweep-and-prune finds candidate body
pairs, GJK<3> detects the overlapping pairs, and EPA<3> supplies penetration
depth and contact normals. A small sequential impulse solver applies restitution
and positional correction in 3D.
Red lines start at the contact point and show the collision normals used by the
solver. The demo is purposely rudimentary: it has no friction, angular collision
impulse, or continuous collision detection.

from =build-demo-3d=. =--bodies N= selects the number of dynamic bodies

* Siconos 3D development demo

=demo-3d-siconos/= uses the same 3D convex meshes as =demo-3d/= and generates
contacts for Siconos' =NewtonEulerDS= dynamical system. CXD broad phase and
GJK<3> validate overlapping pairs, EPA<3> supplies penetration depth and contact
normals, and the demo builds 3D contact Jacobian rows for Siconos' LCP solver.
The demo keeps one Siconos model for its entire run: current contact rows are
updated in place, departing rows are unlinked, and Siconos retains lambda/y state
as the active contact set changes. It advances with fixed 240 Hz Moreau--Jean
steps and a frictionless LCP solver. The demo links only =Siconos::kernel= from
=siconos-devel=; it does not use Siconos Mechanics or its Bullet collision
manager. It currently supports normal impulses and rotational response, but
intentionally omits friction and continuous collision detection.

Evaluate =cxd-create-build-directories= first, then run the following blocks
from =build-demo-3d-siconos=. The =siconos-devel= package is provided by the
Siconos channel pinned in =siconos-2026-08-12.scm=.
=--bodies N= selects the dynamic body count (default: 16), while =--frames N=
permits finite headless runs. Press =Space= to pause, =R= to reset, and =Esc=
to close.

* Siconos development demo

=demo-siconos/= uses CXD's broad phase, GJK, and convex contact geometry to
generate contacts for the same two-dimensional convex meshes. A padded broad
phase keeps nearby pairs, SAT supplies a signed gap, and GJK validates
overlapping pairs. The demo keeps one Siconos model for its entire run:
current contact rows are updated in place, departing rows are unlinked, and
Siconos retains lambda/y state as the active contact set changes. It advances
with fixed 240 Hz Moreau--Jean steps and a frictionless LCP solver. The demo
links only =Siconos::kernel= from =siconos-devel=; it does not use Siconos
Mechanics or its Bullet collision manager. It currently supports normal
impulses and rotational response, but intentionally omits friction and
continuous collision detection.

Evaluate =cxd-create-build-directories= first, then run the following blocks
from =build-demo-siconos=. The =siconos-devel= package is provided by the
Siconos channel pinned in =siconos-2026-08-12.scm=.
=--bodies N= selects the dynamic body count (default: 8), while =--frames N=
permits finite headless runs. Press =Space= to pause, =R= to reset, and =Esc=
to close.
